transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I guess I'm here because I'm having a lot of trouble at work. I work at a meat processing plant right now, which, you know, isn't really what I pictured doing after finishing my bachelor's degree, but the job market is just so weird right now. My roommate actually applied to like forty places and hasn't heard back from a single one, which is crazy because she had a really good GPA and did all these internships. 

But anyway, um, what brings me in is that I keep starting my required stuff at the plant—like the sanitation steps, the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork—and I somehow just... leave out the last parts. Like, I just don't finish them. And I know my job depends on finishing them correctly, especially the sanitation stuff. The industrial bleach they have us use smells so strong, by the way. It gets totally stuck in your clothes. I actually have to wash my work uniform completely separate from my regular clothes, or else everything I own just smells like raw poultry and chemicals. I tried using that scent-booster stuff in the wash, but it just makes it smell like floral bleach. 

But yeah, I'm just really struggling because I keep leaving the last parts of my logs and cleaning steps blank, and I don't really know why I can't just finish them.
Do you remember intending to finish the logs and cleaning steps when you started them?

Um, I mean... I'm not really sure? I don't really remember what I'm thinking when I start them. I just grab the clipboard to do it. Actually, the clipboards they give us are those thick metal ones that open up so you can store extra papers inside? Which makes sense because the plant is always so wet and you don't want the logs getting ruined. But the hinge on mine is completely rusted out, so every time I try to open it, it makes this horrible, loud screeching noise. 

It sounds exactly like the brakes on my car right now, actually. I really need to get my brake pads replaced, but every time I call the mechanic down the street from my apartment, they put me on hold for literally twenty minutes and I just end up hanging up. Like, who has time to just sit on hold listening to elevator music all day? The last time I tried calling, I ended up just reorganizing my entire glovebox instead of waiting. 

...Wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, if I meant to finish the logs when I started them. Yeah, I honestly don't know. I don't really remember intending anything, I just sort of... stop doing it.
Do you often find yourself getting distracted by things around you or thoughts in your head while you're working on tasks?

Um, I don't really know if I'd call it getting distracted? I guess I don't really notice what's happening in the moment. There is a lot going on around me at work, though. Like, the conveyor belts are super loud, and it's freezing in there. They keep the cutting room at like 34 degrees. I actually had to buy these special thermal socks online because my toes were going completely numb by my first break. They're made of merino wool, which is supposed to be the best for moisture-wicking. 

My mom actually knits, and she promised she’d make me a pair of really thick wool socks for work, but she got sidetracked and started this huge cable-knit sweater for my dad instead. Which makes zero sense because he runs so hot. He’s literally that guy who wears gym shorts in December when there's snow on the ground. It drives my mom crazy. She bought him this really nice, expensive parka for Christmas last year and it still has the tags on it hanging in the hall closet. I told her she should just return it, but she lost the receipt, and the store policy is super strict about returns after ninety days... 

Wait, what were you asking? Oh, if I get distracted by thoughts or things around me. I mean, maybe? I honestly don't really know. I just kind of realize later that I didn't finish the thing I was supposed to be doing.
Do you ever find that you can't remember what you were doing or what happened for a short period of time?

Um, like spacing out completely? I'm not really sure. I don't think I have like, missing time or anything like that. But I do lose things all the time if I set them down. Like my phone. I am constantly putting my phone down and having no idea where it went. I actually bought one of those little Bluetooth tracker tags for my keys, which is great, except it doesn't help if I lose the phone itself. 

My roommate has this whole system where she always puts her keys in this little ceramic bowl by the front door. It's actually a really pretty bowl—she made it in a pottery class we took together last summer. Well, I say "we took," but I ended up missing like half the classes because they were on Tuesday nights, and Tuesday is when the local theater does these five-dollar movie tickets. They show older movies, like from the 80s and 90s. We saw *The Princess Bride* there, which I hadn't seen since I was a kid. The seats are super uncomfortable, though, like the springs are totally shot, and the floor is always so sticky... 

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about forgetting things? Yeah, I don't know if I forget what happened, I just... don't really know where my brain goes when I'm supposed to be finishing my logs.
Do you ever find yourself in a situation where you can't recall what just happened?

Um, wait, isn't that kind of what you just asked me? Like, about missing time? Because no, I don't really think I have moments where I completely blank on what literally just happened. It's not like a blackout or anything. 

I mean, my memory isn't great in general, but I don't just forget the last five minutes. Like, I remember my college graduation, even though it feels like a blur because it was raining so hard and we were all just totally miserable. They made us sit outside on the turf field, and they handed out these cheap plastic ponchos that felt exactly like trash bags. Mine actually ripped right down the side because I caught it on one of those white plastic folding chairs. You know the ones they always use for outdoor events? 

My cousin had those exact same chairs at her wedding last year, except she insisted on having the ceremony right on the beach. Which sounds really pretty for pictures, but the chair legs kept sinking into the sand every time someone shifted their weight. My uncle actually tipped completely backward right in the middle of the vows and crushed this massive sandcastle some kids had built earlier that morning. It was so loud, and honestly, her whole wedding was kind of a mess after that. The caterer even brought the wrong cake—it was lemon instead of red velvet, and she hates lemon...

Um, sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? What was the question? Oh, right, recalling what just happened. Yeah, no, I don't think I have that. I just sort of zone out from what I'm supposed to be doing, but I don't forget what actually happened around me, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like your difficulty finishing tasks at work is causing you a lot of stress or problems in your daily life?

Um, yeah, it's definitely causing problems. Like, big problems. We actually just had to have this formal retraining meeting because I keep falling behind, and my coworkers are having to step in and cover parts of my duties just so the line doesn't back up. Which makes me feel terrible, because everyone is already working so hard. 

My coworker, Sarah, she's been there for like five years, and she’s so fast. She actually used to work at this bakery downtown before she started at the processing plant. She said she had to leave because she developed this weird allergy to wheat flour. Can you imagine being a baker and suddenly being allergic to flour? It’s called Baker’s Asthma, I think. She told me she used to make these incredible sourdough loaves that took three days to ferment. I tried making sourdough during the pandemic, like everyone else, but I completely forgot to feed the starter for a week and it grew this fuzzy pink mold that smelled like old gym socks. I ended up throwing the whole jar away. It was a really nice jar, too, one of those thick glass ones with the wire clamp and the rubber seal. I bought a whole set of them at IKEA when I first moved into my apartment because I had this whole vision of organizing my pantry with matching containers...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, the stress at work. Yeah, so, I'm genuinely terrified they're going to move me off the line or just fire me. I feel like I'm becoming a safety concern instead of the reliable worker I want to be. It's just really stressful.
Do you feel anxious or overwhelmed when you think about not being able to finish your tasks at work?

Um, yeah, I do. I feel really anxious about it. It's like this constant weight on my chest because I know I'm falling behind, and I just get so overwhelmed trying to catch up. I mean, the plant is so loud anyway, which doesn't help with the stress. The machinery is just constantly humming and clanking. 

We actually have to wear these heavy-duty earplugs, the kind that are attached to a little plastic cord so they don't fall into the processing line. My cord is bright orange. They come in different colors, though. The supervisors wear blue ones, and the maintenance guys wear green. I kind of wish I could have the green ones because green is my favorite color. I actually just painted my bedroom this really pretty sage green. It took me three weekends to finish because I kept running out of painter's tape. I bought the cheap brand first, and it kept peeling off the wall and letting the paint bleed through onto the baseboards. So then I had to go back to the hardware store and buy the expensive blue tape, and while I was there, I ended up looking at all the different cabinet knobs because I was thinking about updating my kitchen...

Wait, sorry. Anxious, right? Yeah, I just feel really overwhelmed all the time because I can't seem to just finish what I'm supposed to be doing, and I know everyone is noticing.
Do you feel sad or depressed when you can't finish your tasks at work?

Um, sad? I mean, maybe a little disappointed in myself, but I wouldn't say I feel depressed about it. It's more just the stress and the anxiety like I was saying. I don't really get, like, down in the dumps or crying about work. 

I did cry last week, though, but that was because I dropped my phone in the parking lot and the screen completely shattered. It was one of those really bad spiderweb cracks that goes all the way across, and little pieces of glass kept flaking off onto my thumb when I tried to text. I had to take it to one of those kiosk places in the mall to get it fixed. The guy working there was actually super nice, he said he sees it happen all the time. He had this really cool tattoo of a koi fish on his forearm. It was all orange and black, and he said it took like six hours to finish. I've always thought about getting a tattoo, maybe like a little outline of a cat on my ankle, because I had this orange tabby growing up named Marmalade. He was the sweetest cat, but he had this weird habit of chewing on plastic grocery bags. We had to hide all the bags in the house because if he found one, he would just sit there licking and chewing on the handles until they were full of holes. The vet said it was some kind of texture thing, or maybe something in the plastic...

Um, what was I saying? Oh, right, feeling sad. No, I don't really feel depressed about the work stuff. It's just frustrating, you know? But not really sad.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself when you're at work?

Um, outside of my body? No, not really. I mean, I'm definitely in my body, it just feels like my brain is somewhere else sometimes. But I don't feel like I'm floating or watching myself or anything weird like that. 

Speaking of weird, though, the other day on the line, we were processing these huge cuts of beef, and I swear one of them looked exactly like the shape of Texas. Like, perfectly. I almost took a picture of it, but we aren't allowed to have our phones on the floor for hygiene reasons. Plus, my phone still has that new screen from the mall guy, and I bought this super heavy-duty case for it online. It's supposed to be military-grade drop-tested. The package said it could survive a ten-foot drop onto concrete. The case itself is this really bright neon yellow, which I thought would make it easier to find in my purse, but my purse is basically a black hole. I have so many receipts in there. I keep meaning to go through them and sort them out, maybe put them in a little accordion folder. I saw this really cute floral one at Target last week when I went in just to buy toothpaste. I ended up leaving with like eighty dollars worth of stuff, including this candle that smells like pine needles and campfire. It's supposed to be "cabin themed." I've always wanted to rent a cabin in the woods for a weekend, maybe somewhere up in the mountains where you can see the stars...

Wait, sorry. Outside my body. No, I don't get that feeling at all. I'm just regular me, just... distracted me.
Do you ever feel like you're in a dream or a fog when you're at work?

Um, in a dream? No, I don't think so. I don't feel foggy or anything like that. I just feel like I'm trying to focus and it just slips away from me. But definitely not like a dream. 

I actually have really weird dreams at night, though. Like, last night I dreamt I was trying to make a sandwich, but every time I reached for the bread, it turned into a sponge. Like those yellow sponges with the green scrubby side? I use those to clean my bathroom sink because the hard water leaves these white rings around the drain. Our water here is so hard, it completely ruined my favorite electric kettle. The heating element got all crusted over with this chalky white buildup. I tried soaking it in vinegar, which is what my mom always told me to do. My mom is obsessed with cleaning with vinegar. She buys it in those massive gallon jugs from Costco. The last time we went to Costco together, we got one of those huge rotisserie chickens, and we made chicken salad out of it for like three days straight. I like my chicken salad with celery and a little bit of dill, but my mom insists on putting grapes in it, which I just think is so weird. Fruit in mayonnaise? It just doesn't make sense to me. It's like putting pineapple on pizza, which, honestly, I don't hate, but I wouldn't order it on purpose...

Wait, sorry. A fog? No, no fog. Just... just regular awake, just having a hard time paying attention.
Do you feel like you're able to experience a full range of emotions, or do you sometimes feel numb?

Um, numb? No, I definitely feel things. I'm not numb at all. I feel happy, I feel frustrated... I feel all of it. I wouldn't say I'm numb. 

Although, my hands do get kind of numb sometimes at work, but that's just because the meat locker is so incredibly cold. We have to wear these thick insulated gloves, but after a few hours, the cold just seeps right through. I bought these little disposable hand warmer packets, the ones you shake up to activate? You're supposed to put them in your pockets, but I actually tried stuffing them inside my gloves once. It didn't really work out though, because it made my grip all bulky and weird, and you definitely don't want a clumsy grip when you're holding a boning knife. Those knives are so sharp, we have a guy who comes in every Tuesday just to sharpen them. He has this whole setup in the back of his van with these spinning wet stones. It throws sparks everywhere, it's actually really cool to watch. He told me he used to be a chef in a fancy French restaurant before he started his sharpening business. I've never really had fancy French food, just like, croissants from the bakery down the street. They make this almond croissant that is so good, it has this powdered sugar on top that gets all over your shirt when you take a bite. I wore a black sweater there once and I looked like I had dandruff all over my chest by the time I finished it. I had to go to the bathroom and try to brush it off with a wet paper towel, which just made it into a sticky paste...

Oh, wait, you meant emotionally numb, right? Yeah, no, my emotions are totally normal. I definitely feel things. Just... cold hands, sometimes.
Do you ever feel like you're not really connected to what's happening around you when you're at work?

Um, not connected? Like, spaced out? I guess sometimes I'm not totally paying attention to what's happening around me, but I wouldn't say I feel disconnected. It's more like I'm just caught up in my own thoughts and then I realize I haven't been paying attention to the line. 

It's really easy to zone out on the line because the conveyor belt just keeps moving at the exact same speed, all day long. It's this constant hum, like a giant refrigerator. Our refrigerator at home makes this weird rattling noise whenever the ice maker kicks on. It woke me up at like 3 AM the other night, and I thought someone was trying to break in. I actually grabbed my softball bat from the closet. I haven't played softball since high school, but I kept the bat just in case. I was a shortstop, mostly. I really liked the uniform, it was this bright cherry red with white pinstripes. We had to wear these special cleats with plastic spikes because metal ones weren't allowed on the turf field. The turf was always so hot in the summer, you could literally feel the heat radiating through the soles of your shoes. One time, my teammate left her water bottle on the turf during practice, and the plastic actually warped from the heat. It was one of those expensive insulated ones, too, the kind that are supposed to keep ice frozen for 24 hours. I always lose my water bottles. I buy them, and then I leave them on the bus, or at the gym, or just... somewhere. I probably have a graveyard of water bottles scattered across the city. 

Oh, right, connected to what's happening. Yeah, no, I'm connected. I just... I just get distracted by my own head, you know? But I'm definitely there.
Do you ever feel like you're observing yourself from outside your body or like you're in a dream when you're not at work?

Um, outside my body? No, definitely not. I've never felt like I was floating or watching myself or anything weird like that. I'm always just... in my body. Even when I'm not at work. 

I do spend a lot of time outside, though, especially on the weekends. I love hiking, even though I'm really bad at reading trail maps. Last weekend, I went to this state park that's supposed to have these amazing waterfalls, but I ended up taking a wrong turn at this fork in the path and walked for like two hours in the completely wrong direction. I ended up at this weird abandoned stone foundation in the middle of the woods. It looked like an old farmhouse or something. I always wonder about the people who used to live in places like that, you know? Like, did they have a big family? Did they grow their own vegetables? I tried to grow a tomato plant on my balcony last summer, but I kept forgetting to water it. It just shriveled up into this sad brown stick. My roommate was so annoyed because she's like, a plant whisperer. Her room looks like a jungle. She has this huge Monstera plant that's basically taking over the living room. The leaves have these big holes in them, which I guess is normal, but it looks like a giant bug chewed through it. I really hate bugs, especially spiders. If I see a spider, I have to get my roommate to come kill it, or I'll just trap it under a glass and leave it there until she gets home. One time I left a glass over a spider for like three days because she was out of town visiting her parents in Ohio...

Wait, sorry. Observing myself? No, no. I'm just regular me, in my own head. Just... easily distracted, I guess. But definitely not floating around outside myself.
Do you often find yourself trying not to think about your work or the tasks you're struggling with?

Um, trying not to think about work? I mean, I guess I don't really try to actively *not* think about it. I just kind of... don't think about it when I'm not there. Or I think about other things instead. 

Like, when I get home, I'm usually just thinking about what I'm going to make for dinner. I've been trying to get into meal prepping because it's supposed to save so much money, but I can never decide what I want to eat three days in advance. Last week I made this huge batch of quinoa and roasted vegetables, and by Wednesday I was so sick of it I just ordered a pizza. It was from this place down the street that does a really good white pie with ricotta and garlic. I love garlic, but it always makes my breath smell terrible the next day. I have to chew so much gum at work if I eat garlic the night before. I usually buy that wintermint flavor, the one in the blue pack? But sometimes I accidentally buy peppermint and it's just too sharp, you know? It almost burns your tongue. My mom used to grow peppermint in her garden when I was a kid, and it completely took over the whole flowerbed. It's like a weed, it just spreads everywhere. She tried pulling it up, but the roots go so deep. We used to pick the leaves and put them in hot water to make tea, which was actually really nice in the winter...

Oh, but yeah, work. No, I don't really avoid thinking about it. I just... have a lot of other stuff going on in my head, I guess. I'm not avoiding it on purpose.
Do you think your difficulty finishing tasks is more related to feeling anxious or overwhelmed, or to something else entirely?

Um, anxious or overwhelmed? No, I wouldn't say I feel anxious about finishing things. It's not like a panic or anything. It's just... I don't know, it's like my brain just decides it's done with whatever I'm doing before the actual task is done. Like, I'll be halfway through something and then I'm just onto the next thing. 

It happens a lot when I'm trying to clean my apartment. I'll start doing the dishes, and then I'll notice the sponge is getting kind of gross, so I go to the bathroom to get a new one from under the sink. But while I'm under the sink, I see that I'm almost out of that lavender-scented bathroom cleaner. I love that smell, it's so relaxing. I actually bought these lavender sachets to put in my dresser drawers because my clothes were starting to smell kind of musty. I live in this really old building, and the landlord is super cheap, so the ventilation is terrible. The heat is always blasting in the winter, too. The radiators hiss so loudly, it sounds like a snake is trapped in the pipes. I tried to complain about it, but the super just gave me this weird little key to bleed the radiator, and I have no idea how to use it. I'm terrified I'm going to break it and flood the whole apartment with boiling water. Water damage is the worst. My friend had a pipe burst in her ceiling last year, and it ruined her entire collection of vintage records. She had this original pressing of Fleetwood Mac's Rumours that she was so proud of...

Wait, what was the question? Anxious? Oh, right. No, I don't really feel anxious or overwhelmed about finishing tasks. I just... I get sidetracked. My brain just wanders off and forgets to come back to what I was originally doing.
Do you think your difficulty finishing tasks is related to feeling disconnected from yourself or your surroundings?

Um, disconnected from myself? No, not at all. I don't feel disconnected from myself or my surroundings. I'm very aware of my surroundings, actually. Almost too aware sometimes. 

Like at work, I work at this meat processing plant, and it's so loud in there. The machinery is constantly humming and clanking, and it's always freezing cold because of the meat, obviously. I have to wear these thick thermal gloves under my cutting gloves, but my fingers still get numb by the end of my shift. The other day, I was breaking down this huge shipment of poultry, and I kept getting distracted by this one fluorescent light bulb above my station that was flickering. It was just this tiny, rapid little flicker, but it was driving me crazy. I mentioned it to my supervisor, Dave, but he said he didn't even notice it. Dave is nice, but he's always drinking this really strong black coffee that smells like burnt toast. He leaves his empty mugs all over the break room. We have this one microwave in the break room that someone exploded a Hot Pocket in like three weeks ago, and nobody has cleaned it up. The cheese is basically cemented to the glass plate now. I usually just bring cold lunches anyway, like sandwiches or pasta salad, because I don't want to deal with the microwave situation. I make a really good pasta salad with those little tri-color rotini noodles and black olives. I always buy the canned olives, but I can never open them without splashing that weird olive juice all over the counter...

Sorry, what were we talking about? Disconnected? Right, no. I don't feel disconnected at all. I'm definitely present, I just... focus on the wrong things, I guess. But not disconnected.
Do you think you avoid finishing tasks because you don't want to deal with the stress or anxiety that comes with completing them?

Stress or anxiety about completing things? Um, no, I don't think so. It's not like I'm scared of finishing or anything. I just... don't get there. 

Like, I started knitting this scarf last winter. I bought this really chunky, mustard-yellow yarn because I thought it would look so cute with my navy winter coat. I got the coat at this thrift store downtown. It's one of those really heavy, vintage wool ones, you know? It's super warm, but it's so heavy it actually makes my shoulders ache if I wear it for too long. Plus, it has these big brass buttons that are kind of loose. I keep meaning to sew them back on tighter, but I can never find my sewing kit. I think I left it at my old apartment when I moved. My old roommate, Sarah, probably threw it out. She was always throwing my stuff away without asking. Once she threw away this perfectly good sourdough starter I was making. I was feeding it every day, and it was just getting really bubbly and sour-smelling, which is exactly what it's supposed to do! But she said it smelled like old beer and just dumped it down the garbage disposal. The disposal got completely clogged, and the maintenance guy had to come fix it. He was this really grumpy older guy who kept sighing loudly the whole time he was under the sink, and he had this huge wrench that looked like it weighed fifty pounds...

Wait, what did you ask me? Stress? Oh. Yeah, no, I don't avoid finishing things because I'm stressed about the end of it. I just sort of... forget I was doing them in the first place.
Do you think you might be avoiding finishing tasks because it helps you avoid feeling stressed or anxious about something related to the task?

Um, avoiding feeling stressed or anxious? Like, keeping the task unfinished on purpose? No, definitely not. I don't think I do that. It's not a conscious choice to avoid anything. 

Like, I was trying to read this book for a book club I joined. I thought joining a book club would be a good way to meet people, since most of the people at the plant are a lot older than me, and they just want to go home to their families after work. Which I totally get. The work is exhausting. My feet always ache so badly by the time I clock out. I bought these expensive gel insoles for my boots, but they didn't really help. They just made my boots feel too tight, and then I got a blister on my heel that took forever to heal. I had to use those special hydrocolloid bandages, you know the ones? They're like a second skin. They work really well, but they're so expensive for just a little box of them. I usually try to buy store-brand stuff to save money, especially since I'm still paying off my student loans. I got my bachelor's in English literature, which is kind of funny considering I'm chopping up chickens all day now. But I really loved studying literature. I took this one class on Victorian novels, and the professor was so passionate about Charles Dickens. He would actually do all the different voices for the characters when he read aloud in class. It was a little weird, but also really entertaining. He had this crazy wild white hair, kind of like Albert Einstein...

Wait, sorry. What was the question? Avoiding stress? Yeah, no, I don't think I leave things unfinished to avoid stress. I just... I really wanted to finish that book, I just kept putting it down to do something else and then never picked it back up.
Do you think finishing tasks at work might lead to feelings or thoughts that you find unpleasant or difficult to deal with?

Um, unpleasant feelings from finishing tasks at work? No, I wouldn't say that. It's not like I finish cutting up a batch of meat and feel bad about it or anything. I just... I get sidetracked before I'm done. 

Like yesterday, I was supposed to be portioning out these pork loins, and I was doing fine, but then I noticed one of the industrial scales was slightly off-balance. It had this tiny little wobble to it every time I put a piece of meat on it. I tried to fix it by folding up a piece of cardboard from one of the packing boxes and wedging it underneath the leg. But the cardboard kept slipping out because the floor is always a little wet from the spray hoses we use to clean the stations. Those hoses have amazing water pressure, honestly. I wish I had one in my shower at home. The water pressure in my apartment is terrible. It takes me like twenty minutes just to rinse the conditioner out of my hair. I buy this really thick, coconut-scented conditioner because my hair gets so dry, especially in the winter. The cold air just sucks all the moisture right out of it. I tried using coconut oil straight from the jar once, like as a hair mask? But it was a disaster. I couldn't get it washed out, and my hair looked greasy for like three days. I had to wear it in a tight bun the whole time, and my scalp hurt so much by the end of the day. I have this one really soft scrunchie that I usually use, it's made of velvet and it's this deep burgundy color... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Unpleasant thoughts? Oh. No, finishing a task doesn't make me feel bad or anything like that. I just... get derailed by other stuff going on.
Do you think finishing tasks at work might lead to feelings or thoughts that you find unpleasant or difficult to deal with?

Unpleasant feelings from finishing? No, no, it's not that at all. It's actually why I'm here, honestly. I just... I keep starting things and not finishing them, and it's becoming a huge problem. 

Like, what brings me in is that I keep starting the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and somehow I just leave out the last parts. Even when I know my job completely depends on finishing them correctly! It's so frustrating. Like the other day with the sanitation logs, I was filling out the temperature checks, and I remembered I needed a new pen because mine was running out of ink. It was one of those really nice gel pens, the kind that write super smooth? I love those. I usually buy them in bulk online because they're cheaper that way. I have this whole drawer in my desk at home just full of pens and highlighters and sticky notes. I love office supplies. Whenever I go to Target, I always end up in the stationery aisle, even if I just went in for paper towels or something. Target is so dangerous that way. They always have those little dollar sections right at the front, and I always end up buying, like, tiny fake succulents or seasonal hand towels that I don't really need. I bought these Halloween towels with little ghosts on them last year, but then I forgot to put them out until November, so it felt silly to use them...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? The paperwork, right. Yeah, I just... I don't finish the logs or the sanitation steps, even though I know I have to. It's not because I feel bad when I finish them, I just somehow never get to the end.

patient.answer:
Hi. Um, well, I guess I'm here because I'm having a lot of trouble at work. I work at a meat processing plant right now, which, you know, isn't really what I pictured doing after finishing my bachelor's degree, but the job market is just so weird right now. My roommate actually applied to like forty places and hasn't heard back from a single one, which is crazy because she had a really good GPA and did all these internships. 

But anyway, um, what brings me in is that I keep starting my required stuff at the plant—like the sanitation steps, the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork—and I somehow just... leave out the last parts. Like, I just don't finish them. And I know my job depends on finishing them correctly, especially the sanitation stuff. The industrial bleach they have us use smells so strong, by the way. It gets totally stuck in your clothes. I actually have to wash my work uniform completely separate from my regular clothes, or else everything I own just smells like raw poultry and chemicals. I tried using that scent-booster stuff in the wash, but it just makes it smell like floral bleach. 

But yeah, I'm just really struggling because I keep leaving the last parts of my logs and cleaning steps blank, and I don't really know why I can't just finish them.

Which makes sense because the plant is always so wet and you don't want the logs getting ruined. But the hinge on mine is completely rusted out, so every time I try to open it, it makes this horrible, loud screeching noise. 

It sounds exactly like the brakes on my car right now, actually. I really need to get my brake pads replaced, but every time I call the mechanic down the street from my apartment, they put me on hold for literally twenty minutes and I just end up hanging up. Like, who has time to just sit on hold listening to elevator music all day? The last time I tried calling, I ended up just reorganizing my entire glovebox instead of waiting. 

...Wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, if I meant to finish the logs when I started them. Yeah, I honestly don't know. I don't really remember intending anything, I just sort of... stop doing it.

My mom actually knits, and she promised she’d make me a pair of really thick wool socks for work, but she got sidetracked and started this huge cable-knit sweater for my dad instead. Which makes zero sense because he runs so hot. He’s literally that guy who wears gym shorts in December when there's snow on the ground. It drives my mom crazy. She bought him this really nice, expensive parka for Christmas last year and it still has the tags on it hanging in the hall closet. I told her she should just return it, but she lost the receipt, and the store policy is super strict about returns after ninety days... 

Wait, what were you asking? Oh, if I get distracted by thoughts or things around me. I mean, maybe? I honestly don't really know. I just kind of realize later that I didn't finish the thing I was supposed to be doing.

Well, I say "we took," but I ended up missing like half the classes because they were on Tuesday nights, and Tuesday is when the local theater does these five-dollar movie tickets. They show older movies, like from the 80s and 90s. We saw *The Princess Bride* there, which I hadn't seen since I was a kid. The seats are super uncomfortable, though, like the springs are totally shot, and the floor is always so sticky... 

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about forgetting things? Yeah, I don't know if I forget what happened, I just... don't really know where my brain goes when I'm supposed to be finishing my logs.

patient.answer:
Um, wait, isn't that kind of what you just asked me? Like, about missing time? Because no, I don't really think I have moments where I completely blank on what literally just happened. It's not like a blackout or anything.

Like, I remember my college graduation, even though it feels like a blur because it was raining so hard and we were all just totally miserable. They made us sit outside on the turf field, and they handed out these cheap plastic ponchos that felt exactly like trash bags. Mine actually ripped right down the side because I caught it on one of those white plastic folding chairs. You know the ones they always use for outdoor events? 

My cousin had those exact same chairs at her wedding last year, except she insisted on having the ceremony right on the beach. Which sounds really pretty for pictures, but the chair legs kept sinking into the sand every time someone shifted their weight. My uncle actually tipped completely backward right in the middle of the vows and crushed this massive sandcastle some kids had built earlier that morning. It was so loud, and honestly, her whole wedding was kind of a mess after that. The caterer even brought the wrong cake—it was lemon instead of red velvet, and she hates lemon...

Um, sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? What was the question? Oh, right, recalling what just happened. Yeah, no, I don't think I have that. I just sort of zone out from what I'm supposed to be doing, but I don't forget what actually happened around me, if that makes sense.

Um, yeah, it's definitely causing problems. Like, big problems. We actually just had to have this formal retraining meeting because I keep falling behind, and my coworkers are having to step in and cover parts of my duties just so the line doesn't back up. Which makes me feel terrible, because everyone is already working so hard. 

My coworker, Sarah, she's been there for like five years, and she’s so fast. She actually used to work at this bakery downtown before she started at the processing plant. She said she had to leave because she developed this weird allergy to wheat flour. Can you imagine being a baker and suddenly being allergic to flour? It’s called Baker’s Asthma, I think. She told me she used to make these incredible sourdough loaves that took three days to ferment. I tried making sourdough during the pandemic, like everyone else, but I completely forgot to feed the starter for a week and it grew this fuzzy pink mold that smelled like old gym socks. I ended up throwing the whole jar away. It was a really nice jar, too, one of those thick glass ones with the wire clamp and the rubber seal. I bought a whole set of them at IKEA when I first moved into my apartment because I had this whole vision of organizing my pantry with matching containers...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, the stress at work. Yeah, so, I'm genuinely terrified they're going to move me off the line or just fire me. I feel like I'm becoming a safety concern instead of the reliable worker I want to be. It's just really stressful.

Um, yeah, I do. I feel really anxious about it. It's like this constant weight on my chest because I know I'm falling behind, and I just get so overwhelmed trying to catch up. We actually have to wear these heavy-duty earplugs, the kind that are attached to a little plastic cord so they don't fall into the processing line. My cord is bright orange. They come in different colors, though. The supervisors wear blue ones, and the maintenance guys wear green. I kind of wish I could have the green ones because green is my favorite color. I actually just painted my bedroom this really pretty sage green. It took me three weekends to finish because I kept running out of painter's tape. I bought the cheap brand first, and it kept peeling off the wall and letting the paint bleed through onto the baseboards. So then I had to go back to the hardware store and buy the expensive blue tape, and while I was there, I ended up looking at all the different cabinet knobs because I was thinking about updating my kitchen...

Wait, sorry. Anxious, right? Yeah, I just feel really overwhelmed all the time because I can't seem to just finish what I'm supposed to be doing, and I know everyone is noticing.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences emotional distress due to their inability to finish tasks

patient.answer:
Um, sad? I mean, maybe a little disappointed in myself, but I wouldn't say I feel depressed about it. It's more just the stress and the anxiety like I was saying. I don't really get, like, down in the dumps or crying about work. 

I did cry last week, though, but that was because I dropped my phone in the parking lot and the screen completely shattered. It was one of those really bad spiderweb cracks that goes all the way across, and little pieces of glass kept flaking off onto my thumb when I tried to text. I had to take it to one of those kiosk places in the mall to get it fixed. The guy working there was actually super nice, he said he sees it happen all the time. He had this really cool tattoo of a koi fish on his forearm. It was all orange and black, and he said it took like six hours to finish. I've always thought about getting a tattoo, maybe like a little outline of a cat on my ankle, because I had this orange tabby growing up named Marmalade. He was the sweetest cat, but he had this weird habit of chewing on plastic grocery bags. We had to hide all the bags in the house because if he found one, he would just sit there licking and chewing on the handles until they were full of holes. The vet said it was some kind of texture thing, or maybe something in the plastic...

Um, what was I saying? Oh, right, feeling sad. No, I don't really feel depressed about the work stuff. It's just frustrating, you know? But not really sad.

doctor.intent: determine presence of dissociative symptoms

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about depersonalization or dissociative symptoms, which are not covered by my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Um, outside of my body? No, not really. I mean, I'm definitely in my body, it just feels like my brain is somewhere else sometimes. But I don't feel like I'm floating or watching myself or anything weird like that. 

Speaking of weird, though, the other day on the line, we were processing these huge cuts of beef, and I swear one of them looked exactly like the shape of Texas. Like, perfectly. I almost took a picture of it, but we aren't allowed to have our phones on the floor for hygiene reasons. Plus, my phone still has that new screen from the mall guy, and I bought this super heavy-duty case for it online. It's supposed to be military-grade drop-tested. The package said it could survive a ten-foot drop onto concrete. The case itself is this really bright neon yellow, which I thought would make it easier to find in my purse, but my purse is basically a black hole. I have so many receipts in there. I keep meaning to go through them and sort them out, maybe put them in a little accordion folder. I saw this really cute floral one at Target last week when I went in just to buy toothpaste. I ended up leaving with like eighty dollars worth of stuff, including this candle that smells like pine needles and campfire. It's supposed to be "cabin themed." I've always wanted to rent a cabin in the woods for a weekend, maybe somewhere up in the mountains where you can see the stars...

Wait, sorry. Outside my body. No, I don't get that feeling at all. I'm just regular me, just... distracted me.

Um, in a dream? No, I don't think so. I don't feel foggy or anything like that. I just feel like I'm trying to focus and it just slips away from me. But definitely not like a dream. 

I actually have really weird dreams at night, though. Like, last night I dreamt I was trying to make a sandwich, but every time I reached for the bread, it turned into a sponge. Like those yellow sponges with the green scrubby side? I use those to clean my bathroom sink because the hard water leaves these white rings around the drain. Our water here is so hard, it completely ruined my favorite electric kettle. The heating element got all crusted over with this chalky white buildup. I tried soaking it in vinegar, which is what my mom always told me to do. My mom is obsessed with cleaning with vinegar. She buys it in those massive gallon jugs from Costco. The last time we went to Costco together, we got one of those huge rotisserie chickens, and we made chicken salad out of it for like three days straight. I like my chicken salad with celery and a little bit of dill, but my mom insists on putting grapes in it, which I just think is so weird. Fruit in mayonnaise? It just doesn't make sense to me. It's like putting pineapple on pizza, which, honestly, I don't hate, but I wouldn't order it on purpose...

Wait, sorry. A fog? No, no fog. Just... just regular awake, just having a hard time paying attention.

doctor.intent: determine presence of emotional numbing

You're supposed to put them in your pockets, but I actually tried stuffing them inside my gloves once. It didn't really work out though, because it made my grip all bulky and weird, and you definitely don't want a clumsy grip when you're holding a boning knife. Those knives are so sharp, we have a guy who comes in every Tuesday just to sharpen them. He has this whole setup in the back of his van with these spinning wet stones. It throws sparks everywhere, it's actually really cool to watch. He told me he used to be a chef in a fancy French restaurant before he started his sharpening business. I've never really had fancy French food, just like, croissants from the bakery down the street. They make this almond croissant that is so good, it has this powdered sugar on top that gets all over your shirt when you take a bite. I wore a black sweater there once and I looked like I had dandruff all over my chest by the time I finished it. I had to go to the bathroom and try to brush it off with a wet paper towel, which just made it into a sticky paste...

Oh, wait, you meant emotionally numb, right? Yeah, no, my emotions are totally normal. I definitely feel things. Just... cold hands, sometimes.

patient.answer:
Um, not connected? Like, spaced out? I guess sometimes I'm not totally paying attention to what's happening around me, but I wouldn't say I feel disconnected. It's more like I'm just caught up in my own thoughts and then I realize I haven't been paying attention to the line. 

It's really easy to zone out on the line because the conveyor belt just keeps moving at the exact same speed, all day long. It's this constant hum, like a giant refrigerator. Our refrigerator at home makes this weird rattling noise whenever the ice maker kicks on. It woke me up at like 3 AM the other night, and I thought someone was trying to break in. I actually grabbed my softball bat from the closet. I haven't played softball since high school, but I kept the bat just in case. I was a shortstop, mostly. I really liked the uniform, it was this bright cherry red with white pinstripes. We had to wear these special cleats with plastic spikes because metal ones weren't allowed on the turf field. The turf was always so hot in the summer, you could literally feel the heat radiating through the soles of your shoes. One time, my teammate left her water bottle on the turf during practice, and the plastic actually warped from the heat. It was one of those expensive insulated ones, too, the kind that are supposed to keep ice frozen for 24 hours. I always lose my water bottles. I buy them, and then I leave them on the bus, or at the gym, or just... somewhere. I probably have a graveyard of water bottles scattered across the city. 

Oh, right, connected to what's happening. Yeah, no, I'm connected. I just... I just get distracted by my own head, you know? But I'm definitely there.

doctor.intent: determine if patient experiences dissociative symptoms
doctor.question: Do you ever feel like you're observing yourself from outside your body or like you're in a dream when you're not at work?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about symptoms of depersonalization or derealization, which are not part of my ADHD symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Um, outside my body? No, definitely not. I've never felt like I was floating or watching myself or anything weird like that. I'm always just... in my body. Even when I'm not at work. 

I do spend a lot of time outside, though, especially on the weekends. I love hiking, even though I'm really bad at reading trail maps. Last weekend, I went to this state park that's supposed to have these amazing waterfalls, but I ended up taking a wrong turn at this fork in the path and walked for like two hours in the completely wrong direction. I ended up at this weird abandoned stone foundation in the middle of the woods. It looked like an old farmhouse or something. I always wonder about the people who used to live in places like that, you know? Like, did they have a big family? Did they grow their own vegetables? I tried to grow a tomato plant on my balcony last summer, but I kept forgetting to water it. It just shriveled up into this sad brown stick. My roommate was so annoyed because she's like, a plant whisperer. Her room looks like a jungle. She has this huge Monstera plant that's basically taking over the living room. The leaves have these big holes in them, which I guess is normal, but it looks like a giant bug chewed through it. I really hate bugs, especially spiders. If I see a spider, I have to get my roommate to come kill it, or I'll just trap it under a glass and leave it there until she gets home. One time I left a glass over a spider for like three days because she was out of town visiting her parents in Ohio...

Wait, sorry. Observing myself? No, no. I'm just regular me, in my own head. Just... easily distracted, I guess. But definitely not floating around outside myself.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences significant avoidance of thoughts or feelings related to their work difficulties

patient.answer:
Um, trying not to think about work? I mean, I guess I don't really try to actively *not* think about it. I just kind of... don't think about it when I'm not there. Or I think about other things instead. 

Like, when I get home, I'm usually just thinking about what I'm going to make for dinner. I've been trying to get into meal prepping because it's supposed to save so much money, but I can never decide what I want to eat three days in advance. Last week I made this huge batch of quinoa and roasted vegetables, and by Wednesday I was so sick of it I just ordered a pizza. It was from this place down the street that does a really good white pie with ricotta and garlic. I love garlic, but it always makes my breath smell terrible the next day. I have to chew so much gum at work if I eat garlic the night before. I usually buy that wintermint flavor, the one in the blue pack? But sometimes I accidentally buy peppermint and it's just too sharp, you know? It almost burns your tongue. My mom used to grow peppermint in her garden when I was a kid, and it completely took over the whole flowerbed. It's like a weed, it just spreads everywhere. She tried pulling it up, but the roots go so deep. We used to pick the leaves and put them in hot water to make tea, which was actually really nice in the winter...

Oh, but yeah, work. No, I don't really avoid thinking about it. I just... have a lot of other stuff going on in my head, I guess. I'm not avoiding it on purpose.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's symptoms are due to anxiety or another condition

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the difficulty finishing tasks is due to anxiety or feeling overwhelmed, aiming to rule out anxiety disorders or other causes. My symptom profile does not contain an item specifically addressing anxiety or feeling overwhelmed as the cause of my symptoms.

patient.answer:
Um, anxious or overwhelmed? No, I wouldn't say I feel anxious about finishing things. It's not like a panic or anything. It's just... I don't know, it's like my brain just decides it's done with whatever I'm doing before the actual task is done. Like, I'll be halfway through something and then I'm just onto the next thing. 

It happens a lot when I'm trying to clean my apartment. I'll start doing the dishes, and then I'll notice the sponge is getting kind of gross, so I go to the bathroom to get a new one from under the sink. But while I'm under the sink, I see that I'm almost out of that lavender-scented bathroom cleaner. I love that smell, it's so relaxing. I actually bought these lavender sachets to put in my dresser drawers because my clothes were starting to smell kind of musty. I live in this really old building, and the landlord is super cheap, so the ventilation is terrible. The heat is always blasting in the winter, too. The radiators hiss so loudly, it sounds like a snake is trapped in the pipes. I tried to complain about it, but the super just gave me this weird little key to bleed the radiator, and I have no idea how to use it. I'm terrified I'm going to break it and flood the whole apartment with boiling water. Water damage is the worst. My friend had a pipe burst in her ceiling last year, and it ruined her entire collection of vintage records. She had this original pressing of Fleetwood Mac's Rumours that she was so proud of...

Wait, what was the question? Anxious? Oh, right. No, I don't really feel anxious or overwhelmed about finishing tasks. I just... I get sidetracked. My brain just wanders off and forgets to come back to what I was originally doing.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are more consistent with Other Specified Dissociative Disorder (F43.8) or Other Specified Anxiety Disorder (F41.9)

patient.answer:
Um, disconnected from myself? No, not at all. I don't feel disconnected from myself or my surroundings. I'm very aware of my surroundings, actually. Almost too aware sometimes. 

Like at work, I work at this meat processing plant, and it's so loud in there. The machinery is constantly humming and clanking, and it's always freezing cold because of the meat, obviously. I have to wear these thick thermal gloves under my cutting gloves, but my fingers still get numb by the end of my shift. The other day, I was breaking down this huge shipment of poultry, and I kept getting distracted by this one fluorescent light bulb above my station that was flickering. It was just this tiny, rapid little flicker, but it was driving me crazy. I mentioned it to my supervisor, Dave, but he said he didn't even notice it. Dave is nice, but he's always drinking this really strong black coffee that smells like burnt toast. He leaves his empty mugs all over the break room. We have this one microwave in the break room that someone exploded a Hot Pocket in like three weeks ago, and nobody has cleaned it up. The cheese is basically cemented to the glass plate now. I usually just bring cold lunches anyway, like sandwiches or pasta salad, because I don't want to deal with the microwave situation. I make a really good pasta salad with those little tri-color rotini noodles and black olives. I always buy the canned olives, but I can never open them without splashing that weird olive juice all over the counter...

Sorry, what were we talking about? Disconnected? Right, no. I don't feel disconnected at all. I'm definitely present, I just... focus on the wrong things, I guess. But not disconnected.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's difficulty finishing tasks is due to avoidant behavior
doctor.question: Do you think you avoid finishing tasks because you don't want to deal with the stress or anxiety that comes with completing them?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the avoidance of finishing tasks is driven by stress or anxiety, which is a differential diagnosis question (e.g., for anxiety disorders). This does not match any of the ADHD symptoms in the profile.

patient.answer:
Stress or anxiety about completing things? Um, no, I don't think so. It's not like I'm scared of finishing or anything. I just... don't get there. 

Like, I started knitting this scarf last winter. I bought this really chunky, mustard-yellow yarn because I thought it would look so cute with my navy winter coat. I got the coat at this thrift store downtown. It's one of those really heavy, vintage wool ones, you know? It's super warm, but it's so heavy it actually makes my shoulders ache if I wear it for too long. Plus, it has these big brass buttons that are kind of loose. I keep meaning to sew them back on tighter, but I can never find my sewing kit. I think I left it at my old apartment when I moved. My old roommate, Sarah, probably threw it out. She was always throwing my stuff away without asking. Once she threw away this perfectly good sourdough starter I was making. I was feeding it every day, and it was just getting really bubbly and sour-smelling, which is exactly what it's supposed to do! But she said it smelled like old beer and just dumped it down the garbage disposal. The disposal got completely clogged, and the maintenance guy had to come fix it. He was this really grumpy older guy who kept sighing loudly the whole time he was under the sink, and he had this huge wrench that looked like it weighed fifty pounds...

Wait, what did you ask me? Stress? Oh. Yeah, no, I don't avoid finishing things because I'm stressed about the end of it. I just sort of... forget I was doing them in the first place.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's difficulty finishing tasks is due to avoidance of stress or anxiety associated with completion
doctor.question: Do you think you might be avoiding finishing tasks because it helps you avoid feeling stressed or anxious about something related to the task?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the avoidance of finishing tasks is driven by anxiety or stress, which is a differential diagnosis question aimed at ruling out an anxiety disorder, rather than a symptom from the patient's ADHD profile.

patient.answer:
Um, avoiding feeling stressed or anxious? Like, keeping the task unfinished on purpose? No, definitely not. I don't think I do that. It's not a conscious choice to avoid anything. 

Like, I was trying to read this book for a book club I joined. I thought joining a book club would be a good way to meet people, since most of the people at the plant are a lot older than me, and they just want to go home to their families after work. Which I totally get. The work is exhausting. My feet always ache so badly by the time I clock out. I bought these expensive gel insoles for my boots, but they didn't really help. They just made my boots feel too tight, and then I got a blister on my heel that took forever to heal. I had to use those special hydrocolloid bandages, you know the ones? They're like a second skin. They work really well, but they're so expensive for just a little box of them. I usually try to buy store-brand stuff to save money, especially since I'm still paying off my student loans. I got my bachelor's in English literature, which is kind of funny considering I'm chopping up chickens all day now. But I really loved studying literature. I took this one class on Victorian novels, and the professor was so passionate about Charles Dickens. He would actually do all the different voices for the characters when he read aloud in class. It was a little weird, but also really entertaining. He had this crazy wild white hair, kind of like Albert Einstein...

I wish I had one in my shower at home. The water pressure in my apartment is terrible. It takes me like twenty minutes just to rinse the conditioner out of my hair. I tried using coconut oil straight from the jar once, like as a hair mask? But it was a disaster. I couldn't get it washed out, and my hair looked greasy for like three days. I had to wear it in a tight bun the whole time, and my scalp hurt so much by the end of the day. I have this one really soft scrunchie that I usually use, it's made of velvet and it's this deep burgundy color... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Unpleasant thoughts? Oh. No, finishing a task doesn't make me feel bad or anything like that. I just... get derailed by other stuff going on.

patient.answer:
Unpleasant feelings from finishing? No, no, it's not that at all. It's actually why I'm here, honestly. I just... I keep starting things and not finishing them, and it's becoming a huge problem. 

Like, what brings me in is that I keep starting the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and somehow I just leave out the last parts. Even when I know my job completely depends on finishing them correctly! It's so frustrating. Like the other day with the sanitation logs, I was filling out the temperature checks, and I remembered I needed a new pen because mine was running out of ink. It was one of those really nice gel pens, the kind that write super smooth? I love those. I usually buy them in bulk online because they're cheaper that way. I have this whole drawer in my desk at home just full of pens and highlighters and sticky notes. I love office supplies. Whenever I go to Target, I always end up in the stationery aisle, even if I just went in for paper towels or something. Target is so dangerous that way. They always have those little dollar sections right at the front, and I always end up buying, like, tiny fake succulents or seasonal hand towels that I don't really need. I bought these Halloween towels with little ghosts on them last year, but then I forgot to put them out until November, so it felt silly to use them...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? The paperwork, right. Yeah, I just... I don't finish the logs or the sanitation steps, even though I know I have to. It's not because I feel bad when I finish them, I just somehow never get to the end.
